comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Understand phase (orchestrator read, main @ 4ab02ab). Root cause CONFIRMED exactly as described: `update_issue` builds its `Issue` from the issues-table row alone (crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/crud.rs:764) and never hydrates the labels relation before `apply_labels` seeds its diff base (crud.rs:1001-1002), so the before-set is always empty. This predicts all three symptoms: remove-from-empty-set falls into the equal-diff early return (crud.rs:1014-1016); add/set re-INSERT existing rows and hit the labels UNIQUE constraint (crud.rs:1037-1043); the post-transaction hydrated re-read (crud.rs:969-972) shows a correct-looking label set that masks the no-op.

Additional findings beyond the issue text:
1. `content_hash` is unaffected under ANY resolution — spine §1.8 excludes relations (labels/deps/comments) and all timestamps from the hash. So the updated_at question is purely about the timestamp, not hash/import-idempotency.
2. The updated_at asymmetry is in tension with the PRD: FR-1b (the Read/Update requirement, which names "label add/remove/set" as part of update) carries the acceptance criterion "updated_at advances; no-op update is detectable". Precedent: D37's resolved fork FORK-S1 made comment add/edit/redact advance issues.updated_at precisely to feed the stale query; reparent likewise advances it (FR-1b, comment at crud.rs:929-932). Labels are today the only observable mutation excluded (the condition at crud.rs:933). The spine's update_issue clause ("updated_at advances ... only when at least one stored column changes", 01-design-spine.md:1358) omits the label case — this is the spec ruling to make, and it looks like a PRD-vs-spine drift rather than an intended carve-out.
3. Error-leak path: `map_libsql_err` (crates/unblock-storage/src/error.rs:430) routes every non-busy backend failure into `StorageError::Backend` (display "backend failure: {source}") whose sanitized message KEEPS the SQLite text; at the MCP boundary it becomes DATABASE_ERROR carrying that text. The documented posture (error.rs:410-412) hides the TYPE and strips control bytes but deliberately keeps the message — so the global message posture is a separate, GA-frozen design; the label-path fix removes the only expected constraint violation on this path.
4. Regression target: the NFR-16 backend-independent contract suite lives in crates/unblock-storage/src/testkit.rs (update coverage today = contract_update_issue, testkit.rs:152). New red-first cases go there: remove-then-read, add-existing-label, set-overlapping — plus the updated_at ruling pinned whichever way it is decided.

Next: Decide phase — two forks for Miguel (updated_at semantics for label ops; strict vs structurally-idempotent label INSERT), then spec/plan + design review gate before any implementation.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Decide phase — Miguel's rulings (2026-08-04, in-session):

1. updated_at: a genuine label add/remove/set DOES advance issues.updated_at, aligning labels with the two existing precedents (reparent — FR-1b, the PRD Read/Update requirement; and comments — D37's resolved fork FORK-S1, which advances updated_at on comment add/edit/redact to feed the stale query). Recorded as an INLINE AMENDMENT to the spine's update_issue clause (01-design-spine.md:1356-1359) — a refinement of FR-1b's existing "updated_at advances" acceptance criterion, so NO new D-id and no D-range bump. content_hash is untouched in every scenario (spine §1.8 excludes relations and timestamps).

2. Label INSERT stays STRICT (no INSERT OR IGNORE): with the hydration fix the diff guarantees no duplicate insert in normal operation, and the UNIQUE constraint remains a loud integrity tripwire should the diff ever regress. The shipping guard against regression is the contract-suite red-first coverage, not constraint suppression. The global backend-message posture (sanitized SQLite text in DATABASE_ERROR, error.rs:410-412) is a GA-frozen design and stays out of this issue's scope.

Spec/plan going to the design review gate:
a. Spine amendment (01-design-spine.md:1356-1359): the update_issue clause's "updated_at advances ... only when at least one stored column changes" gains the label-relation exception — a real label change advances updated_at exactly as a real reparent does; empty-diff full-skip semantics unchanged.
b. Code fix (crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/crud.rs): inside the update transaction, after issue_from_row (crud.rs:764) and before apply_labels (crud.rs:917), seed issue.labels from the labels table with a single in-tx SELECT (same "ORDER BY label ASC" shape as hydrate at crud.rs:491-493). Labels only — deps/comments are not needed for the diff and the post-tx re-read hydrates fully. The stamping condition at crud.rs:933 gains label_changed so a label-only change stamps updated_at (and harmlessly recomputes content_hash, which excludes relations).
c. Regression coverage, red-first, in the NFR-16 contract suite (crates/unblock-storage/src/testkit.rs): (i) remove-then-read — the label is gone after the round-trip; (ii) add an ALREADY-PRESENT label — idempotent no-op: no error, no event, no updated_at move (this is the case that must go red before the fix); (iii) labels_set overlapping the current set — performs the replacement, events only for the actual deltas; (iv) a genuine label-only change advances updated_at; a label no-op patch does not.
d. Post-merge (Track): remove the stale v1-1 label from ub-lp9.13 through the shipped API — the final acceptance criterion.

Next: design review gate (3 specialist lenses + coordinator, adversarial) over this spec, then implementation in an isolated worktree.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Design review gate: PASS (3 specialist lenses — architecture/spec, Rust correctness, consumer sweep — plus coordinator, adversarial; all four PASS, zero blocking must-fixes). Coordinator independently re-verified every load-bearing claim against main @ 4ab02ab. Key confirmations: red-first is genuine (the contract suite has zero label-op coverage today; the only existing label-update test, behaviour.rs:527-536, asserts nothing the fix changes); no CONTRACT_VERSION bump needed (no schema-byte or error-code movement); sync/export idempotency unaffected (sync_equals ignores updated_at, compares labels sorted); the no-new-D-id ruling matches the PROCESS inline-amendment rule.

Seven advisories carried to the implement team (all non-blocking, first one with must-land force for the verify gate):
1. The spine amendment (01-design-spine.md:1356-1359) must reword the absolute "updated_at advances ... only when at least one stored column changes" and explicitly name BOTH relation exceptions as normative — reparent (shipped code-only in commit 42470c5, currently stated nowhere in the spine — a latent drift this amendment absorbs) and labels (this issue's ruling).
2. Touch the owning crate-plan row (docs/plans/crates/unblock-storage.md:76) in the same commit: in-tx hydrated label diff-base rule, the label-advances-updated_at exception, the four new contract cells.
3. The stamping-condition comment at crud.rs:929-932 must move with the condition change (currently names only row-column/reparent).
4. Label events iterate HashSet differences (nondeterministic order): tests with 2+ adds or 2+ removes in one patch must assert the label-event slice as a set, never an exact sequence.
5. Label events append BEFORE the row update and scalar-field events: a combined label+scalar patch test must expect LabelAdded/LabelRemoved before Updated/StatusChanged.
6. Place the label-seed SELECT after the tombstone guard (crud.rs:768-770), not immediately after the row load, to avoid a wasted query on the tombstone-reject path.
7. Register every new contract fn in run_storage_contract_suite (testkit.rs:146-154) or it never executes; refresh the contract_update_issue doc comment; use exact-equality (pattern at testkit.rs:2085) for the label no-op updated_at assertion.

Next: implement phase — single rust-engineer implementer in an isolated worktree, red-first (the add-existing-label case must be demonstrated red before the fix lands).

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
VERIFY QUALITY GATE, round one — verdict FAIL on two must-fixes, with the engineering itself sound. Four adversarial lenses (code correctness, Rust quality, test design, spec coherence) plus five briefed mutants each in its own worktree, plus two extra mutants a lens invented; coordinator re-derived every blocking claim from source rather than aggregating.

WHAT PASSED, corroborated on disjoint axes rather than taken on the implementer's report. Two lenses independently ran the formatter, clippy with warnings denied, the workspace suite, the doc lint and the layering check; a third ran the four shipped check scripts and the knowledge lint. All green. The seed is straight-line and in-transaction, routes its errors through the same mapper so a failure rolls back, is byte-identical in shape to the read path, sits after the tombstone guard, and the stamping term is correctly gated behind the empty-diff full skip. The spine amendment's two NORMATIVE factual claims were verified at source: commit 42470c5 is indeed where the reparent stamp shipped, it touched one file only, and it is an ancestor of this branch.

THE MUTATION PICTURE, which is the strongest evidence in this gate.
- Reverting the whole fix: killed by all four new cases on BOTH backend legs. A workspace-wide run with that mutant applied showed the storage contract suite is the ONLY target in the repo that catches it — the empirical explanation for why this bug shipped at all.
- Removing only the label term from the stamping condition: killed by exactly one assertion. Both halves of the code change are therefore genuinely pinned. Fragility note, not a gap: that pin rests on the strict greater-than operator; weakening it to greater-or-equal lets the mutant survive.
- Relaxing the strict INSERT to ignore-on-conflict: SURVIVED, and the coordinator judged it a semantically equivalent mutant rather than a coverage hole — with a correct diff base the additions set can only name labels absent from the table, so no conflict is reachable. A compound experiment (relaxed INSERT plus the reintroduced bug) still killed all four cases, proving the relaxation does not blind the suite to the regression the strict-INSERT ruling guards.
- Dropping the sort from the seed query: SURVIVED, and provably unobservable — the seeded vector's only in-transaction consumers collapse it into a set and re-sort, the hash excludes labels, and the returned issue comes from a fresh hydrated read.

THE TWO BLOCKING DEFECTS.
1. The contract suite asserts an event ORDER the interface contract explicitly disclaims. Two new cases pin the exact sequence label-removed then label-added within one patch, while the spine amendment shipped in this same change states that relative order among the label events of one patch is not guaranteed because the diff is a set. Swapping the two reconcile loops reddens exactly those two assertions — so a future backend that reconciles additions first would fail the conformance suite while fully complying with the contract it is graded against. The removals-before-additions claim exists nowhere normative; its only source is a test comment citing the implementation's loop order. The crate plan sides with the spine (it describes that cell as pinning only that label events precede the scalar event). This needs a ruling, taken to Miguel — see the next comment.
2. The per-issue scoping of the query this change ADDS is pinned by nothing. Mutating its WHERE clause to match every row leaves all four new cases and the entire contract suite green on both backends. Every new case has exactly one issue in the database at the moment of its label patch, and the single two-issue point coincidentally yields the asserted events even from a polluted base. A polluted diff base re-creates the exact silent no-op this change fixes, plus spurious removal events. Cheap fix: seed a second issue carrying a distinct label before the ops in one case.

ONE ADVISORY WORTH FIXING IN THE SAME ROUND (a false claim in shipped test prose): an assertion in the updated_at case compares a value to itself, because the loader recomputes the content hash from the loaded fields and never reads the stored column. Its message claims to observe that the stored hash still matches the recompute — which no backend-independent test can observe. A mutant writing a garbage hash column left everything green. The sibling assertion beside it carries the real obligation.

EIGHT FURTHER ADVISORIES, all mechanical: three code comments that overreach or mis-describe pre-fix behaviour; a spine back-reference pointing at a sentence this same amendment deleted; a spine parenthetical still quoting the original tool's skip mechanism rather than ours; a stale line citation on the tombstone guard (pre-existing); the Storage trait doc — the surface every backend author reads — never stating the new relation-stamps-updated_at rule the suite now enforces; and no bullet for this defect in the roadmap's maintenance slot.

A FOURTH USER-VISIBLE CHANGE, beyond the three symptoms in the issue text, surfaced and measured by a lens: pre-fix the removal loop was unreachable, so labels_set was purely ADDITIVE and clearing the label set was a no-op. It is now a real replacement. Correct per the amendment and pinned by the overlap case, but it must be named in the pull-request body and the run-report.

PENDING BY DESIGN, correctly absent and never counted against the change: the knowledge-layer run-report and the tracker re-export, both owned by the Track step on this same branch.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Miguel's ruling on the Verify gate's first must-fix (2026-08-04) — SEPARATE THE TWO QUESTIONS rather than pick a side.

The backend-independent contract suite is loosened to match what the interface contract actually promises: the two label events of one patch are compared as a SET (the scalar event stays pinned last, since that ordering IS spine-guaranteed). The spine text stands as written — relative order among the label events of one patch remains unguaranteed, so no future backend is over-constrained by a conformance suite grading it against an obligation the contract never stated.

And the determinism our OWN implementation happens to have — removals reconciled before additions — is pinned where implementation behaviour belongs: a new case in crates/unblock-storage/tests/behaviour.rs, the file that exists precisely to grade the libsql backend rather than any backend. Nothing is lost on either side: the contract stops over-reaching, and an accidental future swap of the two reconcile loops still turns something red.

Rationale for the split: the contract suite and the interface SSOT that defines conformance were written in the same change and contradicted each other; the fix that merely deletes the assertion would have traded a real guard for nothing, and the fix that promotes the ordering to normative would have widened the contract to buy a property nothing depends on. The third option costs one extra test and keeps both properties.

ROUND-TWO IMPLEMENT SCOPE (loop-back per the process guide's gate-failure rule; this is Verify iteration two):
- Must-fix 1, as ruled above: set-compare in the two contract assertions, plus the new libsql behaviour-suite pin.
- Must-fix 2: pin the per-issue scoping of the query this change adds — seed a second issue carrying distinct labels before the ops so a diff base that ignored the issue scoping is caught. The mutation that widened the WHERE clause to match every row must go RED.
- The tautological assertion in the updated_at case: the loader recomputes the content hash and never reads the stored column, so it compares a value to itself while its message claims otherwise. Delete or reword it; the sibling assertion beside it carries the real obligation.
- The mechanical advisories: two over-reaching code comments, the spine back-reference pointing at a sentence this same amendment deleted, the spine parenthetical still quoting the original tool's skip mechanism rather than ours, the stale line citation on the tombstone guard, and — the one that matters most for a pluggable-backend seam — the Storage trait doc, which every backend author reads and which never states the relation-stamps-updated_at rule the suite now enforces. Plus a bullet for this defect in the roadmap's maintenance slot.
- Every new or changed test must be mutation-proven, not merely written.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
VERIFY QUALITY GATE, round two — PASS from the coordinator on three lenses, then FAIL from the fourth once it was re-run. Full state below, and the process escalation this triggers.

FIRST, AN ORCHESTRATOR DEFECT, stated plainly because it nearly caused a false coverage report. One of the four lenses (documentation fidelity) died mid-run with a connection error. The workflow script filtered the null result and then paired the surviving results with lens names BY POSITION — which silently renames every lens after a dead one. The report labelled "documentation fidelity" was in fact the independent-CI lens, and the one labelled "independent CI" was the fresh-eyes lens (it gave itself away by naming its own scratch directory). So the documentation axis appeared covered and was not, and the gate coordinator was handed two misattributed reports. The lens was re-run in isolation; the fix for the pattern is to tag each result with its own identity at the source rather than re-deriving it by index.

WHAT THE THREE LENSES THAT DID RUN ESTABLISHED — coordinator verdict PASS, no must-fixes, every closure re-derived from source rather than accepted on report.
- Both round-one blockers are closed faithfully to Miguel's ruling. The loosened assertions still pin the length, both event types, both payloads, and the scalar event LAST; only the label-versus-label sequence was dropped, which is exactly the half the spine declines to guarantee. The backend fact is pinned in the libsql-specific behaviour file with a four-element comparison — two events per group, so no lucky pair and no interleaving satisfies it.
- The lens that failed this change last round attacked the real risk of a loosening round with four mutants of its own: appending an extra event, deleting an event, corrupting a payload, and flushing the scalar events early. All four go RED. The set-compare kept its teeth.
- The per-issue scoping case genuinely kills the mutant that survived before, in both directions.
- THE FLAKE QUESTION IS CLOSED WITH NUMBERS, which the previous round could not do. One lens ran 25 behaviour executions with the change and 60 with the new test removed: the same failure-rate band on both sides. Another ran 15 full workspace executions across three legs, including one carrying 40 times this change's marginal load, and got ZERO failures. Structurally the change adds exactly ONE in-memory store to a default workspace run. Not attributable to this work; a pre-existing class already documented in the source.

WHAT THE RE-RUN DOCUMENTATION LENS FOUND — verdict FAIL on one defect, which I verified myself at source before accepting it.
docs/plans/00-roadmap.md, the new maintenance-slot bullet, asserts "It newly rejects nothing — every input it changes was previously accepted and silently mishandled". That is FALSE for two of the four input classes, and the bullet contradicts itself twice: nine lines above it says an already-present label add was "turning an idempotent call into an opaque backend error", and four lines above it says "a duplicate label add stops erroring". Those inputs were REJECTED loudly, not silently mishandled. The bullet's CONCLUSION survives (this files with the bug fixes, not with the ratified behavioural breaks) — only its justification clause is false. It is release-notes text for v1.0.1, and it currently hides the one error-to-success transition this cut carries, which is the most user-visible change a release note owes its reader.
Same sentence, separate advisory: the user-visible list omits that labels_set now genuinely REPLACES — its clear-and-narrow arm was unreachable, so clearing the label set was a no-op.

WHAT THAT LENS CONFIRMED AS SOUND, on the axis nobody else covered: every sentence of the new Storage::update_issue trait doc checked against the code and against the spine and found true, including that it promises exactly the event ordering the spine guarantees and declines exactly the one it does not; the whole amended spine clause read end to end and internally consistent after two rounds, with both of its NEW line citations accurate; a full drift sweep across the docs, the knowledge layer, every crate source and doc comment, the agent-facing wiring file and the README returning ZERO surviving statements that contradict the final behaviour; the engine's mirror of the reconciliation matching storage; and the no-new-decision-id posture correctly stated in all three documents with no decision-range string moved anywhere. It also verified that NO citation which was accurate before this change became stale because of it.

STANDING ADVISORIES ACROSS BOTH ROUNDS, none blocking, listed so the scope decision can be made with them in view: a comment in the new scoping case claims the scoping holds for WRITES too, but that half is vacuous — with a correct diff base that step never reaches a DELETE; the reconcile DELETE's own per-issue scope is consequently pinned by nothing (a mutant dropping it survives); labels_set to the EMPTY set is exercised nowhere in the workspace, and it is the last uncovered consequence of this very defect, reachable from the wire; the crate plan overstates the payload coverage of one cell half and carries a derived count inside an enumeration; a rhetorical aside in the spine over-generalises; and roughly twelve stale crud.rs line citations sit across the product doc, the spine, the crate plan and an engine test — all PRE-EXISTING, of which this change fixed exactly one.

PROCESS POSITION: this is the second Verify iteration to close without a clean pass, so per the gate-failure rule it escalates to Miguel rather than looping further. The rounds are converging sharply — round one found two structural test defects, round two found one false clause in release-notes prose — but the rule is the rule, and the remaining scope question is genuinely his.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
VERIFY GATE, final round — PASS on the repair, with three sweep-up defects handed to the Track step rather than looped back.

WHAT WAS REPAIRED, and it passed. The two false statements in the interface contract are gone, and I verified both at source rather than accepting the verdict. The pre-fix narrative now says plainly that NOT SKIPPED did not mean LANDED, then separates the three shapes: an add of genuinely absent labels landed its rows and events while losing only the timestamp stamp; a patch naming an already-present label died on the label table's primary key and rolled its whole transaction back, landing nothing at all, not even its row columns; and no pre-fix update ever removed a label, because the reconcile iterates before-minus-current and an empty before-set makes that empty by construction — which is also why the set operation was purely additive and clearing was a no-op. The normative paragraph no longer permits a count to be derived, and it now states the two behaviours it was missing: that a caller's set DROPS the labels it does not list, and that the empty set really clears. Both retired framings have zero live hits repo-wide.

AN ORCHESTRATION FAILURE WORTH RECORDING. Three of the five agents in this round died mid-run on a usage limit, leaving the gate with one lens. The run was resumed rather than restarted: the writer and the completed lens replayed from cache and only the three dead agents ran live. Separately, the one lens that had completed ran without its safety classifier available, so its claims were re-verified by hand before being relied on. Neither cost any work.

THE COORDINATOR FOUND WHAT ALL THREE LENSES MISSED, which is the interesting part. It ran its own sweep across the whole branch instead of trusting the sites the lenses named, and found that the same retired claim survived in TWO further documents plus a rotted count in a third:
1. The release-notes bullet asserts that the post-transaction re-read "masked both" symptoms. False, and self-contradicting within one sentence: its own preceding clause says the already-present add turned an idempotent call into an opaque backend error. An error is the loudest possible outcome, not a masked one — that path rolled back and no re-read ever ran on it. Confirmed branch-authored: the sentence does not exist on main.
2. The storage crate plan carries the same defect condensed, having dropped the disambiguator that the code comment it was condensed from still keeps ("the remove is the SILENT one") — so the code comment is correct and the plan's condensation is not.
3. The contract-suite doc comment says the label half lives in "the four" cases below. SIX are registered. This branch wrote the numeral and then grew the list past it — so without the fix the pull request would ship, in a single diff, the rule and its violation, because the interface-contract text on this very branch now says these consequences are stated as a list and never as a count, precisely because the list grows.

WHY THIS PASSED RATHER THAN FAILED, and I agree with the reasoning: the commit under review is correct and complete for what it set out to do. All three defects belong to EARLIER commits on the same branch that this round did not sweep. Failing would have looped a correct commit back to implementation, and this was already the fourth round against a process rule that caps loops at two. They are one-clause edits and they land on the same branch, in the same pull request, through the Track step — which is a team in its own right, so nothing is being hand-waved.

THE PATTERN THIS TASK ACTUALLY TAUGHT, worth more than the bug itself: the production code passed every gate round unchanged after the first. Every defect found from round two onward was PROSE claiming more than was true — tests asserting they graded things they did not, and documents describing behaviour that never existed. The repo already hunts this class in one narrow form, the derived count; this task shows the same disease in ordinary sentences, and it survived three adversarial rounds in the highest-authority document precisely because no lint reaches there.

Track is now running: the three sweep-up fixes, five further one-clause advisories the gate asked to land in the same pull request (including bringing the implementor-facing trait documentation in line with what the suite now hard-gates), the knowledge-layer run-report, and the tracker re-export.

description:
Found 2026-08-03 while doing ordinary tracker upkeep on ub-lp9.13 (correcting a stale release label). Live on `main` @ 503835d — the MCP server is wired as `cargo run --bin unblock mcp` (`.mcp.json`), so this is the current tree, not a stale binary.

THREE OBSERVED SYMPTOMS, all on `issue {action:"update"}`, all reproduced twice — once on the real issue ub-lp9.13, once on a clean ephemeral probe created and hard-deleted for the purpose:
1. `labels_remove` NEVER removes. It returns `isError:false` with the unchanged label set in the response and does not move `updated_at`. On the probe, an issue created with `["probe-alpha","probe-beta"]` still carried both after `labels_remove:["probe-beta"]`. A caller has no way to tell the operation did nothing — this is the same silent-acceptance class as the D42 argument-boundary family (unknown fields discarded with `isError:false`).
2. `labels_add` of an ALREADY-PRESENT label hard-errors, and leaks the backend verbatim: `{"code":"DATABASE_ERROR","message":"backend failure: SQLite failure: \`UNIQUE constraint failed: labels.issue_id, labels.label\`"}`. Adding a label is naturally idempotent; instead it is a trap. The raw SQLite text crossing the boundary is a second, independent defect — the layering contract forbids backend error leakage, and the taxonomy is owned by `unblock-error` at the L7 boundary.
3. `labels_set` fails the same way whenever ANY member of the new set is already attached, so it never performs the replacement it advertises. It cannot be used as a workaround for symptom 1.

CONSEQUENCE: over the MCP surface a label can be added but NEVER removed, and a set that overlaps the current one cannot be applied at all. ub-lp9.13 is currently stuck carrying both `v1-1` and `v1-0-1` for exactly this reason — the stale label cannot be removed through the shipped API, which is how this was found.

ROOT CAUSE (established by reading, and it predicts all three symptoms exactly). `crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/crud.rs:993` `apply_labels` computes its diff from `issue.labels`, seeding `before` at :1001-1002. But the `issue` it receives was built at :764 by `issue_from_row(&row)` from a `SELECT` over the `issues` table alone, inside the transaction; labels live in a separate `labels` table and are hydrated only by the separate relation query at :488-493, which this path never calls before the diff. So `before` is ALWAYS empty. Therefore: a removal is removal-from-an-empty-set, the diff comes out equal, `:1014` returns `false` and nothing happens (symptom 1); an add or a set lands every element in `current.difference(&before)` and re-INSERTs rows that already exist, hitting the UNIQUE constraint at :1037-1043 (symptoms 2 and 3). The full hydration happens only AFTER the transaction, at :969-972, which is why the response shows a correct-looking label set and hides the no-op.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION, needs a spec ruling rather than an assumed fix: a genuine label change does not advance `updated_at`. At :925 a label change counts as a change for the empty-diff skip, but at :933 the stamping condition is `!builder.is_empty() || parent_changed` — labels are excluded, while a reparent was deliberately included with a comment explaining why. Adding a NEW label to the probe left `updated_at` at its creation value. Decide whether that asymmetry is intended (labels may sit outside `content_hash` as a relation) or is a second bug — a modification invisible to `updated_at` is invisible to staleness queries and to anything keyed on it.

### Acceptance Criteria
- The update transaction diffs against the issue's ACTUAL label set, so removal removes, add is idempotent, and set replaces.
- No SQLite text can reach the client from a label operation; any residual failure surfaces through the owned error taxonomy.
- The `updated_at` question is decided explicitly and the decision is recorded, not left implicit in the condition at `crud.rs:933`.
- Regression coverage in the storage contract suite (the cross-implementation suite required by NFR-16) pins all three: remove-then-read, add-twice, and set-overlapping. A test that only adds distinct labels passes today and proves nothing — the add-an-existing-label case is the one that must go red before the fix.
- The stale `v1-1` label on ub-lp9.13 is removable through the shipped API once fixed, and is removed.
title: Bug: label removal is a silent no-op and label add/set hard-error on any existing label — the update path never hydrates labels

description:
Found 2026-08-03 as a by-product of diagnosing a bench-gate failure on the ub-lp9.13 branch (pull request 436). The failure itself was runner degradation and the re-run went green, but the investigation measured the two create benchmarks properly and found they are not measuring what their names say.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken on an isolated machine with interleaved builds (8 rounds of 40 iterations, controls with byte-identical code agreeing, so the harness is calibrated). Inside the timed region of `storage_create/insert` on main: the insert itself costs 0.114 ms, while `drop(storage)` costs 2.625 ms and `drop(tempdir)` 1.799 ms. So roughly 97% of the reported sample is teardown, not the operation being named. The cause is mechanical: the benchmark routine takes its setup tuple BY VALUE, so the drop happens inside the timed closure rather than after it. `engine_create/mint` has the same shape.

WHY IT MATTERS, beyond tidiness. A ceiling on a number that is 97% filesystem teardown cannot detect a regression in the operation it claims to guard — a create path could get several times slower and the gate would barely move. It also makes the gate maximally sensitive to runner I/O noise, which is exactly how it produced a false red: on the degraded run, `engine_create/mint` read 19.077 ms against a main baseline of about 2.1 ms, while the operation itself had not changed at all (measured at +2%). A gate that mostly measures the filesystem will keep crying wolf, and each false red costs a real investigation.

THE FIX, as the diagnosis proposed it: have the routine borrow rather than consume, so the drop falls outside the timed region — either by returning the setup value from the closure or by using the borrowing variant of the batched iterator. Both create benchmarks need it.

CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST BE PLANNED, not discovered: correcting this changes the measured numbers by roughly two orders of magnitude, so BOTH ceilings and the recorded baseline entries must be re-derived in the same change — `xtask/src/bench_gate.rs` and `xtask/bench-baseline.json`. Re-deriving them is the point: the new ceiling would guard the create path for the first time.

WORTH CHECKING AT THE SAME TIME, since the shape may not be unique to these two: every other benchmark using the batched iterator with a per-iteration workspace should be inspected for the same by-value teardown.

### Acceptance Criteria
- The timed region of both create benchmarks excludes teardown, demonstrated by measuring the operation and the drops separately and showing the reported mean now tracks the operation.
- Both ceilings and the baseline entries are re-derived from the corrected measurement, in the same change.
- A deliberate slowdown injected into the create path moves the reported number proportionally — the property the current benchmarks lack, proven by execution rather than asserted.
- Any other benchmark sharing the by-value teardown shape is either fixed or explicitly recorded as inspected and sound.
title: Bench: the two create benchmarks measure teardown, not the operation (~97% of the sample is drop)

description:
Found 2026-08-04 by the Verify gate on ub-lp9.27, and deliberately scoped OUT of that change (Miguel's ruling) because mixing a cross-cutting sweep into a point bug fix is not wanted and because the durable fix is a script rather than another manual pass.

Roughly twelve live citations of `crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/crud.rs` point at line ranges that no longer hold the symbol they name. All are PRE-EXISTING — verified against main @ 4ab02ab, where they were already wrong — so nothing here was introduced by ub-lp9.27, which fixed exactly one of them.

THE THREE FAMILIES, each verified at source during that gate:
- The tombstone-patch guard is cited as `crud.rs:332-334` at `docs/plans/01-design-spine.md:1917`, `:2357`, `:2612` and at `crates/unblock-engine/tests/writes.rs:703`, `:756`, `:765`. That range is a D45 dependency-target existence comment; the guard is around `crud.rs:770-773`. The spine now DISAGREES WITH ITSELF about the same guard, because the ub-lp9.27 amendment corrected the one citation inside the clause it was editing.
- `apply_reparent` is cited as `crud.rs:972-1032` at `docs/plans/01-design-spine.md:1254` and `:1405` and at `docs/PRD.md:128`; it is around `crud.rs:1126`. Worth noting that the stale range now points INSIDE the updated_at stamping block, so it reads as a live pointer to unrelated code rather than as an obviously dead one.
- `row_exists` is cited as `crud.rs:1328` at `docs/plans/01-design-spine.md:1409` and `:1589`, at `docs/PRD.md` and at `docs/plans/crates/unblock-storage.md:79`; it is around `crud.rs:1510`. Plus `crates/unblock-storage/tests/behaviour.rs:951` citing apply_reparent at `crud.rs:625-668`.

WHY A SCRIPT RATHER THAN A SWEEP. Line citations rot on every insertion above them, silently, and this family has now rotted through at least three unrelated changes. A one-off re-citation pass buys a few months and then fails the same way — which is exactly the class the repo already decided to make executable elsewhere (the derived-count rule in the process guide, and the `scripts/checks/` family that enforces it). The check should resolve each cited file-and-line to an expected symbol and fail when it does not match, so the CI job that already runs that family catches the next rot at the commit that causes it.

### Acceptance Criteria
- A check in the existing `scripts/checks/` family resolves every `crud.rs` citation in the doc corpus and in test prose to the symbol it names, and exits non-zero when a citation no longer resolves.
- It is wired into the same required CI job as its siblings.
- Its own failure mode is proven, not asserted: mutating one citation makes the script exit non-zero on exactly that row.
- All twelve known-stale citations above are corrected in the same change, and the spine no longer disagrees with itself about the tombstone guard.
- The design deliberately addresses whether a citation-resolving check can be spelling-independent, or whether it needs an explicit registry of (file, line, expected symbol) rows — and records the reasoning, since a registry is itself a thing that can rot.
title: Stale crud.rs line citations across PRD, spine, crate plan and an engine test — replace manual re-citation with an executable check

description:
Surfaced 2026-08-04 while verifying ub-lp9.27, and scoped out of it because nothing in that change causes it.

`LibsqlStorage::open_in_memory` opens a shared-cache URI, which mutates SQLite's process-global shared-cache registry. Its own doc comment (around `crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/mod.rs:326-346`) already documents the consequence: an internal open-lock serializes open-against-open but explicitly "cannot cover the window where an open races a concurrent large shared-cache transaction", and the class is described as "a load-marginal artifact of the shared-cache registry, not a bug this constructor can safely immunize against".

The practical cost is that a REQUIRED CI job can go red for a reason that has nothing to do with the change being tested, and a reviewer then has to prove a negative under time pressure. That is exactly what happened during the ub-lp9.27 verification, and closing it took two independent controlled experiments.

WHAT WAS MEASURED THERE, worth keeping because it bounds the problem rather than merely naming it:
- Every observed failure landed at the store OPEN (the fixture helper around `crates/unblock-storage/tests/behaviour.rs:29`), never at an assertion, and always in tests unrelated to the change under test.
- One controlled comparison: 1 failure in 25 behaviour-suite executions with the change, and 1 in 60 with the change's new test removed — the same rate band on both sides, i.e. no attributable effect.
- A second: 15 full workspace executions across three legs, one of them carrying 40 times the marginal load the change added, with ZERO failures — the class could not be reproduced at all on that machine.

The doc comment already prescribes a direction (route heavy or high-concurrency work through the file-backed constructor instead). The open question this issue exists to answer is whether the behaviour suite as a whole should migrate, or whether a narrower fix reaches the same result.

### Acceptance Criteria
- A decision is recorded on whether the behaviour suite migrates off the shared-cache in-memory constructor, with the reasoning — including what the in-memory constructor is buying today (speed, isolation) and what migrating would cost.
- Whatever is chosen is measured rather than asserted: a failure-rate comparison across enough executions to distinguish the rates involved, given the observed base rate is on the order of one in tens of runs.
- If the class survives by design, the required job's failure is made SELF-EXPLAINING — whoever meets a red run learns from the output that this class exists and how to tell it apart from a real regression, rather than having to rediscover the doc comment.
title: The shared-cache in-memory store can redden the required workspace-test job for reasons unrelated to the change under test

description:
Raised 2026-08-04 by the Verify gate on ub-lp9.27, scoped out of that change because it is a question about a rule rather than a defect in the fix.

The interface spine states normatively that the label reconcile INSERT stays STRICT — never ignore-on-conflict — so that the label uniqueness constraint remains a loud tripwire if the diff base ever regresses. That rule was a deliberate ruling on ub-lp9.27, and the reasoning behind it stands.

The problem is that the rule is pinned by NOTHING, and appears to be unpinnable by construction. A mutation relaxing the INSERT to ignore-on-conflict left both the contract suite and the behaviour suite green, and the gate coordinator judged it a semantically EQUIVALENT mutant rather than a coverage hole, verified by reading the code: with a correct diff base the additions set can only ever name labels absent from the table, so no conflict is reachable and the two spellings cannot differ in observable behaviour. A compound experiment confirmed the tripwire still works as intended — relaxing the INSERT while ALSO reintroducing the diff-base bug still reddened every relevant case, through different assertions.

So the honest position is that the rule buys a louder failure mode in a future regression, and that no test can distinguish it from its alternative today. That is a legitimate thing for a codebase to conclude, but it should be CONCLUDED rather than left as an unexamined gap — otherwise a future reader finds a normative rule with no enforcement and reasonably assumes someone forgot to write the test.

### Acceptance Criteria
- A decision is recorded on whether the strict-INSERT rule is testable: either a test lands that genuinely distinguishes strict from ignore-on-conflict, or the conclusion that it cannot be distinguished through the trait surface is written down with the reasoning.
- If it cannot be, the code comment beside that INSERT says so explicitly — that it is the only guard, and why the rule is kept anyway — so the absence of a test reads as a considered position rather than an omission.
- The spine sentence is left consistent with whatever is decided.
title: Decide whether the spine's strict label INSERT rule is testable at all — and if not, say so where the only guard lives

description:
Found 2026-08-06 by the ub-cnv (D47) Verify gate, whose adversarial lens measured it rather than reasoned about it. Miguel scoped it OUT of D47 and into its own issue: it is PRE-EXISTING, not a regression, and the real fix touches a transport seam D47 deliberately left alone.

MECHANISM, confirmed at source by two independent readers. rmcp drives our transport's receive() as one arm of a tokio select! with no priority (rmcp-1.7.0/src/service.rs:805, the receive arm at :813), so that future is DROPPED whenever another arm wins the race. Both out-of-band replies our transport emits are written INSIDE receive(): the pre-existing -32700 parse-error arm, and the -32600 arm D47 added (crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs). On cancellation the reply is therefore never written — and the frame is lost too, because the next iteration begins by clearing the line buffer. There is no retry and no queue.

MEASURED, once, by one harness, and recorded as such rather than dressed up: 0 of 40 replies lost on an idle connection; 25 of 40 lost with four concurrent requests in flight; 39 of 40 lost with eight. The pre-existing -32700 arm on main loses at the same rate (35 of 40 at eight), which is what establishes this as a property of the transport rather than of D47.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN D47, and why that was right. It is outside the decided scope of that change; the severe case D47 exists to remove — the frame that killed the process before the handshake — occurs by definition with zero requests in flight, the regime measured at zero losses; and fixing it properly means changing where the transport writes, which would drag the pre-existing -32700 arm along with it or leave two different behaviours in one file. D47 discloses the residual instead of claiming a guarantee it does not hold under load (docs/PRD.md, the D47 row; crates/unblock-mcp/src/wire.rs module documentation).

DO NOT let the mutex around the write half be mistaken for a defence: it buys byte-atomicity between concurrent writers, which is a different property entirely from surviving future cancellation.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The loss is reproduced deliberately and the rates are REPLICATED by a second harness, since the recorded figures are single-run and single-harness.
- The transport stops writing replies from inside receive(): the reply is parked on the transport itself, or pushed to whatever sink send() already uses, so a cancelled receive() cannot swallow it.
- BOTH out-of-band arms move together — the -32600 envelope-id arm and the pre-existing -32700 parse-error arm — so the file does not end up with two behaviours.
- A regression cell drives concurrent traffic and asserts the reply arrives; it must fail on the current code.
- The residual disclosures land closed: the D47 decision row, the transport module documentation, and both roadmap cards stop naming this as open.
title: Bug: an out-of-band transport reply is lost whenever rmcp cancels the receive() future under concurrent request traffic

acceptance_criteria:
REWRITTEN at the Decide/Spec boundary and CORRECTED at the design Review gate (2026-08-06). The original four criteria are superseded because two were unsatisfiable-as-meant: "all four Err sources" is vacuously satisfiable (two of the four return sites are structurally unreachable), and "stdout carries only JSON-RPC frames for the whole process lifetime" literally covers `unblock mcp --help`, which the Decide phase ruled explicitly out. The substance is unchanged and nothing is narrowed.

1. CHANNEL. On `unblock mcp`, no failure of the command may put a non-frame byte on stdout. Proven over the REACHABLE failure cases, named individually rather than counted: the walk-up workspace miss (`NOT_INITIALIZED`, exit 2), an explicit `--dir`/`UNBLOCK_DIR` at a non-workspace (`CONFIG_ERROR`, exit 7), a rejected `UNBLOCK_OUTPUT_FORMAT` (`CONFIG_ERROR`, exit 7), a database newer than the build (`SCHEMA_MISMATCH`, exit 2), a corrupt database (`DATABASE_ERROR`, exit 2), and a first frame that is neither `initialize` nor `ping` (`INTERNAL_ERROR`, exit 1 — `ping` is answered pre-handshake and is NOT a failure case; see the gate comment). The two unreachable return sites (`Session::open`, which fails only on a feature the CLI hard-codes off, and the teardown, whose semaphore is never closed) are documented as unreachable rather than covered by a cell that can only pass vacuously.

2. POSITIVE LANDING, not only the absence. Every case above must ALSO be shown to land the full structured document on stderr — `code`, `message`, `retryable`, and `hint` where the code carries one. A frame-only negative alone is insufficient and is explicitly rejected as an acceptance route: on the pre-run-loop cases stdout is legitimately empty, so a negative-only assertion stays green under a delete-the-diagnostic mutation. That vacuity class is what hid this defect.

3. EXIT CODES UNMOVED. Every code listed in criterion 1 is the code that ships. A failed handshake keeps exit 1; the reconciliation with D40 is that D40's exit-0 carve-out covers the pre-`initialize` DISCONNECT only and is untouched, and that after the GA tag a one-to-zero flip on this surface would be a semver-relevant CLI change under D35.

4. MUTATION PROOF. Every cell added or inverted names the concrete source edit that turns it red, and that edit is actually applied and observed to turn it red — a coverage claim is not accepted on inspection. This binds especially the swapped-sink mutation, which compiles and survives every in-process cell, and is why a spawning end-to-end cell is required alongside the injected sinks.

5. THE INVERSIONS ARE HONEST, AND FAIL LOUD. The two shipped cells that assert the defect as correct (`crates/unblock-cli/tests/mcp_lifecycle.rs:429-440` and `:602-606`, coupled at `:578-583`) are rewritten to assert the new channel while still pinning what they protected — the exit code, the never-swallowed clause, and the D47 coupling. No cell is weakened to make it pass. AND the harness drain handles are retained and joined before any negative stdout snapshot: without that, an inverted "stdout is empty" assertion goes GREEN on a lost race where today's positive assertion goes red, turning this change's own regression pins fail-silent.

6. THE CLASS THAT HID IT IS CLOSED. The shared stream guard (`crates/unblock-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:324-326`) requires a top-level `jsonrpc` member rather than merely valid JSON, that guard is itself driven by a self-test (a guard nobody drives is a guard that can be deleted), and the shared spawn helper (`:111-117`) scrubs `UNBLOCK_OUTPUT_FORMAT` — without which any new frame-only cell passes vacuously from a host shell that sets it.

7. NFR-14 RECONCILED, D48 LANDED. The decision ships as D48 with reciprocal cross-references to the D38 clause it supersedes, the NFR-14 carve-out stated over the PROPERTY (a subcommand whose stdout is a protocol channel) and not over a command name, and the D-range bump at every live site PROCESS section 3 enumerates. `unblock mcp --help` is ruled out of scope IN THE DECISION TEXT, and the carve-out is carried into NFR-14 and the README too — not only into the decision row a casual reader never reaches.

8. NOTHING ELSE MOVES. No other subcommand's bytes change stream; no MCP contract byte, `CONTRACT_HASH` or `ErrorCode` moves; no layer edge changes. Proven, not asserted.

9. THE GATE SCRIPT. D48 mints `scripts/checks/d48-stdout-channel-claims.sh`, following the D44/D45/D46/D47 precedent, in the IMPLEMENTATION commit together with the prose that enumerates it as a required step (ci-cd section 2.1, PROCESS section 3, the CI workflow). It pins what prose alone cannot: the residual-issue landing duty and the single-caller invariant the mechanism leans on.

10. RESIDUALS DISCLOSED, not implied closed. Four are named in the decision row as deliberately open: `ub-kp7` (a first frame that is neither `initialize` nor `ping` still kills the server), `ub-b1a` (the message still embeds an unbounded `Debug` rendering of client bytes), `ub-c5o` (`output::emit_report` writes to stdout with no notion of a stdout-owning command — latent), and `ub-5v5` (no response-size cap, so a large frame may be written truncated — reasoned from source, never reproduced). Unmeasured classes — a blob following valid frames via a panic in the spawned serve task, Windows, and a non-pipe descriptor 1 — are stated as unmeasured rather than covered.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR 439 (2026-08-07, rebase-merge, tip 9adc2cb) as decision D48. The `unblock mcp` structured error no longer lands on STDOUT, which on the MCP stdio transport is the JSON-RPC framing channel: the exit boundary now knows that a command owns stdout as a protocol channel and writes the FULL structured document — code, message, retryable and hint — to stderr instead. Exit codes are unmoved. The defect was five routes wide, not the one its report named, and the likeliest was the most mundane: a workspace open that fails before the startup binding line, leaving stdout with the blob and stderr completely empty. Measured after the fix: all six reachable routes put zero non-frame bytes on stdout with the document on stderr, newline-terminated, at exit 2/7/7/2/1/1; a pre-initialize ping is still answered into a normal handshake; clean EOF still exits 0; version and migrate still write to stdout. 17 named mutations killed including the swapped-sink one that survives every in-process cell, and an invented-mutation pass found five further unpinned claims, all closed. Both gates FAILED and neither was closed by a clean re-pass — the design gate by an orchestrator-applied third pass under the PROCESS section 5 escalation, the Verify gate by a narrow independent recheck plus orchestrator measurement, both on Miguel's explicit ruling; this is recorded rather than smoothed over. Four residuals disclosed rather than absorbed: ub-kp7 (a first frame that is neither initialize nor ping still kills the server), ub-b1a (the relocated message still carries an unbounded Debug rendering of client bytes, raised to high priority once the one-for-one amplification into a persistent log sink was measured), ub-c5o (emit_report still writes to stdout unclassified, latent), ub-5v5 (no response-size cap, reasoned from source and never reproduced). ub-gwe was raised in passing and is unrelated.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
Orchestrator orientation (2026-08-06), off main at 7790db0 (post-D47/PR 438), binary `target/debug/unblock` rebuilt.

Measured with a raw stdio probe: one spawn per case, frames fed on stdin, stdout and stderr captured separately, every stdout line parsed and checked for `"jsonrpc":"2.0"`. Script kept out of the repo. Cases are named, not lettered, so this comment stays readable on its own.

WHAT THE PROBE FOUND — the blob is NOT confined to the handshake path.

1. `pre-handshake notification first` (`notifications/cancelled` as the very first frame): stdout gets one non-frame line `{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"mcp server error: failed to start the MCP server: expect initialized request ..."}`, exit 1. This is the issue's reproduction, still live.

2. `pre-handshake non-initialize REQUEST first` (`tools/list` with id 7): IDENTICAL blob on stdout, exit 1. This CORRECTS the issue description, which says a clean non-initialize request in that position is answered normally and exits 0. It is not: rmcp's `expect_next_message` rejects ANY non-`initialize` message in the initialize slot. The trigger is therefore not the degradation to a notification — it is any first frame that is not `initialize`.

3. `no workspace` (UNBLOCK_DIR pointing at a non-workspace): stdout gets a non-frame `{"code":"CONFIG_ERROR",...}` line, exit 7. This is a PRE-run-loop failure and, in practice, the most likely real-world one — it is what an MCP client sees whenever it spawns the server outside a workspace.

4. `corrupt db` (`.unblock/unblock.db` containing text): stdout gets a non-frame `{"code":"DATABASE_ERROR",...}` line, exit 2. Also pre-run-loop.

5. `EOF before any frame`: stdout empty, exit 0 — D40 holds.

6. `full handshake then EOF`: one valid frame, exit 0 — the healthy path is unaffected.

7. `garbage non-JSON first line`: answered in-band with a `-32700` parse-error frame, exit 0 — the D47/D43 wire seam behaves.

8. `pre-handshake notification with -o plain`: stdout EMPTY, the same error rendered as `error[INTERNAL_ERROR]: ...` on stderr, exit 1. So the stream is chosen purely by the resolved output format, and `UNBLOCK_OUTPUT_FORMAT=plain` is today an accidental workaround for the defect.

MECHANISM. Every error returned by `commands::mcp::run` reaches `run_with` → `exit::into_exit(err, fmt)` (crates/unblock-cli/src/lib.rs:78), and its json/robot arm (crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:135-145) writes the structured payload to STDOUT. The resolved format defaults to Json (crates/unblock-cli/src/output.rs:173). So the blob is not one path but FOUR error sources on the mcp command, all sharing one renderer: the workspace open, `Session::open`, the run loop, and the teardown — the first two of which the issue text only suspected.

Everything the command emits deliberately already goes to stderr: the D39 workspace-binding line (crates/unblock-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:273), the D38 `emit_diagnostic` line (crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:171), tracing. The single leak is the terminal `into_exit` render.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR SCOPE. The exit-code question the acceptance criteria raise is separable from the channel question, and the channel question is the wider of the two: fixing only the handshake case would leave the two pre-run-loop cases (3 and 4) writing the same non-frame bytes onto the framing channel. The Understand phase is briefed to enumerate the remaining stdout writers exhaustively (panic path, rmcp internals, libsql, any direct print) rather than assume these four are all.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
DECIDE phase closed (2026-08-06). Understand ran as a four-lens team plus coordinator; the consolidated map was re-verified by the orchestrator against source before anything was put to Miguel. Miguel resolved four forks; the orchestrator ruled the rest. Both gates are still ahead.

WHAT THE UNDERSTAND PHASE CHANGED ABOUT THE PROBLEM
- The likeliest real-world hit is NOT the handshake: it is the workspace open failing (crates/unblock-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:267), which puts a CONFIG_ERROR blob on stdout with exit 7 and leaves stderr COMPLETELY EMPTY — the D39 binding line at :273 runs only after the open succeeds. A schema-newer database and a corrupt database land the same way with exit 2, and a bad UNBLOCK_OUTPUT_FORMAT value is reported, self-referentially, in the format the resolver defaulted to.
- Of the four return sites, only two are reachable: Session::open fails only on FeatureNotWired for sync, which the CLI hard-codes off (crates/unblock-cli/src/dispatch.rs:48), and the teardown fails only on a poisoned write permit whose semaphore is never closed anywhere in the engine. An acceptance criterion phrased as "covers all four sources" would be satisfiable vacuously.
- Two SHIPPED test cells assert the defect as correct and must INVERT: crates/unblock-cli/tests/mcp_lifecycle.rs:429-440 (asserts the payload on stdout carries INTERNAL_ERROR, docstring at :404-406 calling it the FR-11 anchor) and :602-606, coupled by design at :578-583. The reason the suite never caught this: the only stream guard, crates/unblock-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:324-326, panics with the message "every stdout line must be JSON-RPC framing" but only calls serde_json::from_str — and the blob is valid JSON.

MIGUEL'S FORK RESOLUTIONS
1. Mechanism — the exit boundary learns that a command owns stdout. A predicate read where the parsed command is still in scope (crates/unblock-cli/src/lib.rs:73-75) is threaded into into_exit, whose machine-format arm then writes to stderr for such a command. Chosen over forcing the plain format (which would silently break the FR-13 precedence that pick_cli_format exists to implement) and over having mcp report its own errors (which would add a second exit-code-computing site against the rule that the CLI owns the cast, crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:1-3).
2. Payload — the FULL structured JSON moves to stderr, not the one-line human form. Reason: it keeps the hint member, which is exactly what the schema-mismatch case (D46) carries, and it stays machine-readable for an MCP host that captures the child's stderr.
3. Resilience — the server surviving a non-initialize first frame is REAL work but its OWN task: ub-kp7. ub-og3 stays a pure channel fix.
4. Exit code — a failed handshake KEEPS exit 1. D40 records that after the GA tag a one-to-zero flip on this surface is a semver-relevant CLI change under D35, and D40 covers only the ConnectionClosed case, not this one. Consequence: the exit-code question does not move, so the new decision has a single clause and needs no second D-id.

ORCHESTRATOR RULINGS (Miguel invited objection; none raised)
5. `unblock mcp --help` is OUT of scope, explicitly rather than silently: it writes 846 bytes of prose to stdout with exit 0, but the server never starts, so the framing channel is never live; routing it to stderr would depart from clap and from every other subcommand. The decision states this rather than leaving it to re-open at the Verify gate. (Verified in passing that `unblock mcp --version` is a usage error to stderr with exit 2, correcting one lens that claimed otherwise.)
6. The regression test does BOTH: a spawning end-to-end cell AND an injected sink on into_exit. In-process capture is otherwise impossible — into_exit writes through std::io::stdout().lock(), bypassing libtest capture, and forbid(unsafe_code) with no libc dependency rules out redirecting the descriptor. The sink also closes the sibling hole at crates/unblock-cli/src/logging.rs:46, where mutating the writer to stdout survives the entire suite today. The test must assert a POSITIVE stderr landing, not only the frame-only negative: for the pre-run-loop cases stdout is legitimately empty, so a negative-only assertion stays green under "delete the diagnostic". UNBLOCK_OUTPUT_FORMAT must also be scrubbed in the shared spawn helper (crates/unblock-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:111-117 scrubs three variables but not that one) or a host shell setting it makes the new test pass vacuously.
7. The attacker-controlled Debug rendering in the message — the other half of D47 clause 8(iii) — goes to its own issue, ub-b1a. Control characters are already escaped by sanitize_message; what is unruled is the absence of a length cap.
8. Pre-run-loop failures KEEP their own 0-8 exit codes (7 for config, 2 for database). Only the channel moves. This preserves the D38 scope boundary, which explicitly places a failure raised before the run loop outside the cancellation's consequences.
9. The shared harness guard at crates/unblock-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:324-326 is hardened in this change to require a jsonrpc member, not merely valid JSON. It does not by itself catch this defect (the blob is written after the run loop, past that read path) but it closes the class that hid it, and roughly forty inherited cells then obey it.

DECISION IDENTITY — a NEW D-id (D48), not an addendum. PROCESS §3 puts a refinement whose intent is preserved on the addendum arm, expressly "not a reversal". This IS a reversal: docs/PRD.md:121 and docs/plans/01-design-spine.md:3333 affirmatively rule that FR-11's always-valid-JSON-on-stdout rule binds the unsignalled error path. PROCESS §3 then sends a clause reversal that falls out of a new decision to that decision's own D-id. Two independent supports: the pre-run-loop failures occupy ground no shipped decision row covers, and D47 clause 8(iii) has already classified this as a separate defect with its own issue. Consequences: reciprocal cross-references at both rows, and the D-range bump from D1..D47 to D1..D48 at all seven live sites in the same spec commit — CLAUDE.md:17, docs/plans/ci-cd-and-distribution.md:65, xtask/src/doc_lint.rs:455, and the range knobs of the four shipped required check scripts. The historical range strings inside docs/plans/implementation-plan.md:40,:53,:90 are past bump records and must NOT be re-bumped. A gap to close in the same commit: ub-og3 has no normative name anywhere — both docs/PRD.md:130 and the roadmap say "a separate defect with its own issue" without the id.

RESIDUALS CARRIED INTO SPEC/PLAN, not silently dropped: whether a blob can follow VALID frames (only via a panic in rmcp's spawned serve task, reasoned from source and never measured — if unreachable the acceptance criterion's "including teardown failures" has no live referent and should say so); the truncated frame above two mebibytes with no response-size cap, a different defect on the same channel; Windows, where every measurement here is macOS; and a non-pipe or closed descriptor 1, where write failures are swallowed by design.

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
DESIGN REVIEW GATE — closed PASS after two adversarial rounds plus an orchestrator-applied third pass, under a PROCESS section 5 escalation Miguel ruled on directly (2026-08-06). Branch ub-og3-mcp-stdout-channel, spec-only, uncommitted at the time of writing.

ROUND 1 — FAIL, 15 must-fixes and 10 should-fixes. Four adversarial lenses (code claims, doc cascade, design soundness, test adequacy) plus a coordinator, run against a throwaway worktree so the live tree was never touched. The gate earned its cost: the findings were real and several were the exact class this repo has paid for before — prose asserting more than is true.

THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERED MOST, and it was the orchestrator's own error, repeated into three artifacts before the gate caught it. The claim "any first frame that is not `initialize` kills the server" is FALSE. A pre-`initialize` `ping` is ANSWERED and the server lives on to complete a normal handshake. Established twice over: read in rmcp 1.7.0 service/server.rs:170-204, where the loop answers a `PingRequest` at :175-189 and CONTINUES (the code comment cites the MCP lifecycle specification, which permits ping before initialize), breaks on any other Request at :191, errors on any non-Request at :193, and errors on a non-`initialize` Request at :200-204; and measured directly — a ping frame first is answered with an empty result, a following `initialize` completes, exit 0. The true class is "any first frame that is neither `initialize` nor `ping`, Request or Notification". The false version had already reached the orientation comment above, the ub-kp7 issue and the D48 row; all three are corrected.

OTHER ROUND-1 FINDINGS WORTH RECORDING, because each is a defect a lint cannot reach:
- NFR-14 and the README were left stating an ABSOLUTE ("stdout carries framing only") that a shipped green test falsifies — `unblock mcp --help` writes clap prose to stdout, which the decision's own clause deliberately excludes. The carve-out existed in the decision row but not in the two sentences a reader meets without it.
- A specified test guard whose body could never execute: every call site asserted stdout was empty immediately after calling the framing predicate, so replacing the predicate with an empty body left the whole matrix green.
- The two inversions would have converted a fail-LOUD race into a fail-SILENT one. The harness spawns a detached stdout drain thread and never joins it; today's positive assertion goes red when that race is lost, but the new "stdout is empty" assertion goes GREEN — so the headline mutation could survive on the stdout half of this change's own regression pins. The remedy is to retain and join the handle before any negative snapshot.
- A derived count wrong again ("all four return sites"; there are three — the fourth exists only as an error SOURCE, a different noun), a roadmap citation that named a slot holding something else, and the ub-b1a residual anchored in a file containing no `Debug` formatting at all.

ROUND 2 — FAIL, 4 must-fixes, all one-clause prose edits, two of them NEWLY INTRODUCED by round 2 itself. That is the honest signal: each pass fixes findings and writes new prose, and new prose carries new claims.

ESCALATION AND CLOSURE. PROCESS section 5 escalates after two iterations rather than looping. Miguel ruled the orchestrator applies the four by hand, since the judgement was already done and only the typing remained. All four verified against source first, then applied:
1. the row that MINTS ub-b1a still anchored it at the serialiser rather than at its origin, contradicting the line immediately below it in the same diff;
2. one crate-plan cell declared both the old and the new function arity;
3. `version` was named among the cells that kill the blanket-classifier mutation — it is an exit-0 SUCCESS report through `output::emit_report`, which this decision does not touch, so it stays green and pins nothing. Verified in passing that `doctor` IS a genuine killer (migrate_doctor.rs:490-513 asserts a structured error on stdout), so only `version` was wrong;
4. the deferral of the new gate script to the implementation commit is CORRECT but was justified by a false rule; the true rule is that a required-STEP ENUMERATION must not list a step absent from the tree, while ordinary prose may name a planned one.

RE-VERIFIED after the hand pass: doc-lint OK (19 docs, 6 classes clean), the five required check scripts green (d43, d44, ub-lp9.25, d46, d47), check-layering green, and the two hand-fixed false strings confirmed gone.

DEFERRED TO THE IMPLEMENTATION COMMIT, inherited by the Implement phase and checkable at the Verify gate: the new gate script scripts/checks/d48-stdout-channel-claims.sh and the prose that names it in ci-cd section 2.1, PROCESS section 3 and the CI workflow — following the verified D47 precedent, where the PRD named the script in the spec commit and the enumeration edits landed with the implementation.

FOUR RESIDUALS NOW NAMED IN THE DECISION ROW RATHER THAN IMPLIED CLOSED: ub-kp7 (the server still dies on a first frame that is neither `initialize` nor `ping`), ub-b1a (the message still embeds an unbounded `Debug` rendering of client bytes), ub-c5o (`output::emit_report` writes to stdout with no notion of a stdout-owning command — latent, since no live path reaches it from `mcp`), and ub-5v5 (no response-size cap, so a large frame may be written truncated — reasoned from source and never reproduced, and stated in that register).

comments.author: ramosmig
comments.text:
VERIFY GATE + TRACK (2026-08-07). Branch ub-og3-mcp-stdout-channel, six commits. Read the gate outcome with its deviations in view — they are stated, not buried.

VERIFY ROUND 1 — FAIL, six must-fixes. Three adversarial lenses (code, tests, systems-and-security) plus a coordinator, each in its own worktree. Five findings were the class that has caught this change at every single gate: prose or a docstring claiming more than is true. One was a real test defect.

THE REAL ONE, and the orchestrator MEASURED it rather than taking the gate at its word. The self-test that claimed to pin `wait_for` joining its drain threads did not pin it, and said in its own docstring that it "reads the SYNCHRONISATION, not its outcome". It read the length of the handle vector — which `join_drains` empties with `drain(..)` whether or not it joins. Replacing `handle.join()` with `drop(handle)` was applied and the WHOLE unblock-cli crate stayed green at cargo exit 0. That was the SECOND escape of this same pin: the earlier mutation round closed "delete the call" and never covered "gut the body". The repaired cell now uses a grandchild that writes a second AFTER the child exits, so an unjoined drain provably has not read those bytes — an observation the mutation cannot fabricate, unlike a side effect it reproduced exactly. Re-measured after the fix: both mutations turn it red at cargo exit 101, and so does gating the join on a successful exit (the new fixture exits 1, which the old one did not).

THE FIVE PROSE ONES: a claim that one cell was the only in-process guard when three are; stdout purity claimed for "the WHOLE command" and "EVERY path" when `--help` is carved out by decision and a shipped test asserts it; a derived count wrong in both halves; roughly twenty stale file:line anchors in the decision row, one pointing at a different function entirely; and a gate-script row satisfiable by a doc comment rather than by the production line it claimed to pin.

MIGUEL RULED ONE SCOPE QUESTION, on measured evidence. The relocated payload is length-unbounded: a 5,000,000-byte method name produces 5,000,422 bytes on stderr while stdout stays at zero. D48 amplifies nothing — those bytes went to stdout before, equally unbounded — but it changes the SINK: under the D31 child-per-client topology the host captures the child stderr into logs that PERSIST, whereas an unparseable line on the framing channel was transient. The clip stays out of scope (clause (3) freezes the payload bytes and a cell asserts them; the fix belongs in another crate) but is now DISCLOSED in the decision row, and ub-b1a was raised to high priority and carries the measurements.

THE NARROW RECHECK. A full re-gate would not fit the session budget, so Miguel ruled a single independent read-only lens scoped to "are the six genuinely closed". It confirmed all six — and found THREE FURTHER FALSE SENTENCES written by the repair round itself, including an exclusivity claim of exactly the kind the round existed to retire, inside the paragraph that retired it. All three verified against source by the orchestrator and corrected by hand.

PROCESS DEVIATIONS, stated plainly because a reader must not mistake this for a clean gate pass:
- The design Review gate was closed by an orchestrator-applied third pass rather than a third team round, under the PROCESS section 5 escalation, with Miguel deciding.
- The Verify gate FAILED and was not re-passed by a full independent gate. What stands in its place is the narrow single-lens recheck above plus the orchestrator's own measurements. That is weaker than a gate pass and is not being presented as one.
- Track ran solo rather than as a team, for budget.

WHAT THE ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED PERSONALLY, not by report: the drain mutations dying; all 32 line-ranged anchors in the decision row resolving, and the load-bearing one pointing at the real machine-format arm; each of the four named prose corrections present in source; the three new false claims; and the end-to-end behaviour — six reachable failure routes with zero non-frame bytes on stdout, the full document on stderr newline-terminated, exit codes unmoved at 2/7/7/2/1/1, `ping` still answered into a normal handshake, clean EOF still exit 0, and version and migrate still writing to stdout.

TRACK. The `.unblock/issues.jsonl` re-export landed with the run-report in one commit — and it is what turned scripts/checks/d48-stdout-channel-claims.sh from exit 1 to exit 0, because the script required the four residual issues to exist in the git-backed record. The gate minted for this decision went green for the right reason rather than by being weakened. Run-report: .knowledge/wiki/runs/2026-08-07-mcp-stdout-framing-channel.md.

RESIDUALS, all open and named in the decision row: ub-kp7, ub-b1a, ub-c5o, ub-5v5. Two coverage gaps were left open and REPORTED by the implementer rather than closed silently, on the grounds that no shipped sentence misdescribes them.
