description:
Found 2026-08-05 by the ub-cnv Understand phase and verified directly by the orchestrator. Miguel scoped it OUT of ub-cnv and into its own issue: ub-cnv's fix removes one WAY of reaching this, but the defect itself is about which channel the error is written to, and that is reachable by other routes and touches D40's teardown contract.

REPRODUCED. Start the server and make the very first frame anything that decodes to a notification — for instance a frame carrying an undecodable request id, which is exactly the ub-cnv class. rmcp fails the handshake with "expect initialized request", and the process then writes this to STDOUT:

  {"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"mcp server error: failed to start the MCP server: expect initialized request, but received: Some(Notification(JsonRpcNotification { ... }))","retryable":false}

and exits 1. A clean non-initialize request in the same position is answered normally and exits 0, so the trigger is the degradation to a notification, not the absence of a handshake.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT ON ITS OWN. On the MCP stdio transport, stdout is the JSON-RPC framing channel: every byte on it is supposed to be a JSON-RPC frame. This blob is not one. A client reading the stream gets an unparseable line where a frame is expected — the server's own diagnostic corrupts the channel it is diagnosing. The repo's own rule (NFR-14) is structured output to stdout and diagnostics to stderr, but for the mcp subcommand the structured-output channel IS the protocol, which the generic CLI error renderer does not know.

The path is crates/unblock-cli/src/exit.rs:133-141 rendering a StructuredError in the json output format, reached because the mcp server-start error maps to ErrorCode::InternalError, whose exit code is 1 (crates/unblock-error/src/code.rs:315). Adjacent decision: D40 already settled the exit code for EOF-before-handshake; this is the neighbouring question of what the mcp path may write, and where.

INVESTIGATE FIRST. Establish every way the mcp subcommand can write a non-frame byte to stdout, not just this one. The handshake-failure path is the one observed; there may be others (panic paths, early workspace errors, the update path).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Every non-frame diagnostic on the mcp path goes to stderr; stdout carries only JSON-RPC frames, for the whole lifetime of the process including startup and teardown failures.
- The exit code for a failed handshake is decided explicitly and reconciled with D40, which already fixed the EOF-before-handshake code — either it rides D40's reasoning or the difference is stated.
- A regression test asserts stdout is frame-only on the failure path, and it fails if the blob returns.
- Whatever ships is reconciled with NFR-14, whose "structured to stdout" wording does not anticipate a subcommand whose stdout is a protocol channel.
title: Bug: `unblock mcp` writes its structured-error blob onto STDOUT — the JSON-RPC framing channel — on every startup failure and on a failed handshake

description:
Observed 2026-08-06 by the ub-cnv (D47) implementer while running the full local gate on branch ubcnv-envelope-id-reject. Reported rather than swept: it is unrelated to that branch, which touches no crate below the MCP layer.

SYMPTOM. `cargo insta test --check --workspace --all-features` exited 1 on the unblock-storage test `libsql::tests::open_in_memory_parallel_first_write_stress`, failing with `BackendOpaque("SQLite failure: bad parameter or other API misuse")` raised around crates/unblock-storage/src/libsql/mod.rs:1081. The same test was then re-run five times in isolation and passed 5/5, and a full re-run of the whole suite was green — so it is intermittent, not a deterministic break.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NUISANCE. This is the in-memory parallel first-write stress test, i.e. it exercises exactly the contention path that NFR-3 and the M0 contention lab exist to protect, on a data-integrity tool. An intermittent SQLite API-misuse error on that path is either (a) a genuine race in how the backend opens or serializes the first write against concurrent openers, or (b) a defect in the test's own harness. Which of the two it is has not been established, and the difference is the difference between a test bug and a storage bug.

DO NOT assume it is the test. The comparable case already in the tracker (ub-jyf) IS a generator defect, and the temptation is to file this beside it and move on; the failure mode here is different in kind — a backend error surfacing from the library, not a property-test assertion.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The failure is reproduced deliberately (a loop over many runs, ideally under load or with a stress count raised) rather than waited for.
- Established from the libsql API contract which call is being misused and by whom: the production open/write path, or the test harness.
- If it is a production race: fixed at the storage layer, with a contention case added to the Storage contract suite (NFR-16).
- If it is a harness defect: fixed in the test, with the reason recorded so the next reader does not re-suspect the backend.
- The test is deterministic-green across a high repeat count locally.
title: Flaky: libsql open_in_memory_parallel_first_write_stress intermittently fails with SQLite "bad parameter or other API misuse"

description:
Found 2026-08-07 by the ub-gwe Verify gate, by MUTATION. Nothing is broken today; this is a latent defect in a required check's reasoning, and it will bite at a future decision cascade rather than now.

THE RATIONALE, quoted from scripts/checks/d44-create-deps-claims.sh (the comment block just above the live-range knob): "WHY ONE OF THE THREE IS ROW-ANCHORED AND THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT. A file-level token check proves the literal is SOMEWHERE in the file. That is sufficient for CLAUDE.md and xtask/src/doc_lint.rs, which carry exactly one occurrence each (the bump site itself)." The same claim is restated on the row itself, which labels the CLAUDE.md entry as sound at file level "because this file carries exactly ONE occurrence, the bump site itself".

WHAT MUTATION SHOWED. Appending a SECOND occurrence of the live decision-range literal to CLAUDE.md left that script — and all four sibling range scripts — at exit 0. Changing the literal to a STALE range did fire the row check red, as designed. So the check enforces PRESENCE of the live range, and nothing enforces the uniqueness the rationale rests on.

WHY THAT MATTERS, precisely. The rationale is not decoration: it is the argument for why this site is checked at file level instead of being row-anchored. The comment itself records that this exact reasoning already failed once elsewhere — the ci-cd document also described the pin in prose, and reverting the normative statement to the previous range left the file-level check green because the prose satisfied it. That is the same failure mode, and the CLAUDE.md site is protected from it only by the accident that nothing has yet added a second mention. A future decision cascade that adds one — entirely plausibly, since these cascades touch prose sites by design — would leave the file-level check green while the bump site itself went stale.

STATE TODAY, verified: CLAUDE.md carries exactly one occurrence, in the document-map row. The ub-gwe change that surfaced this adds none, and the bullet it rewrites contains no range literal.

RELATED: the sibling finding that no executable check anchors the CLAUDE.md hard rules at all (issue ub-lg7). Both concern the same unprotected file and may share one fix.

### Acceptance Criteria
- The site is either ROW-ANCHORED (so the check binds to the document-map row rather than to the file), or the uniqueness the rationale rests on is itself made executable (the check fails when a second occurrence appears), or the rationale is rewritten to claim only what is enforced. Any of the three is acceptable; leaving a required check justified by an unenforced premise is not.
- Whichever is chosen is proven by mutation, in both directions: adding a second occurrence, and staling the live one, each produce the intended result.
- The same question is answered for the sibling site in xtask/src/doc_lint.rs, which the identical rationale covers with the identical wording — do not fix one and leave its twin.
- The comment block that carries the reasoning is left consistent with the code in the same change, since its whole purpose is to tell the next editor why the shapes differ.
title: Chore: the CLAUDE.md D-range check enforces only PRESENCE while its rationale claims "exactly one occurrence" — a future cascade can defeat it silently

description:
Found 2026-08-07 by the ub-gwe Verify gate, measured independently by two lenses in separate private checkouts, and scoped OUT of that change: it fails identically on pristine main and with the change applied, so nothing in ub-gwe causes it.

WHAT IT IS. scripts/knowledge/tests/landing-verify.sh was written at the .knowledge layer's landing (the run-report at .knowledge/wiki/runs/2026-07-23-knowledge-layer-landing.md records it as the executable replacement for a set of self-falsifying prose greps, and records it reporting all checks OK at that time). It is an ALLOWLIST-based check: it asserts that certain tokens appear only in the files that are supposed to carry them.

WHAT IT REPORTS TODAY, verbatim, exit non-zero:
  landing-verify: FAIL — token 'knowledge-lint' appears in unexpected file: scripts/checks/d44-create-deps-claims.sh
  landing-verify: FAIL — token '.knowledge' appears in unexpected file: .github/workflows/knowledge-gardener-reminder.yml
  landing-verify: FAIL — token '.knowledge' appears in unexpected file: scripts/checks/ub-lp9.25-dangling-blocker-claims.sh
  landing-verify: FAIL — a live same-commit sentence lacks the run-report clause in its 2-line window

WHY IT WENT RED WITHOUT ANYONE NOTICING. It is wired into NO workflow. The required doc-lint job runs the six scripts under scripts/checks/ plus the doc-lint, the knowledge-lint and the run-report-gate selftest, and never calls this one; a repo-wide search finds it named only in its own file and in that one descriptive run-report. So its allowlist rotted as later, entirely legitimate work added files that mention .knowledge and knowledge-lint — the gardener-reminder workflow and two check scripts — and no job was there to catch the drift at the commit that caused it.

THE DECISION THIS ISSUE EXISTS TO FORCE, because both readings are defensible and leaving it in the tree unread is the only option that is not: either the script has served its purpose (it verified a one-off landing that is now long past) and should be RETIRED, or the property it guards is still worth guarding and it must be wired into the required job — in which case its allowlist becomes maintained state and every future file that legitimately mentions those tokens has to update it. A checker that no job runs is worse than no checker, because its green is never observed and its red is never seen.

### Acceptance Criteria
- The fork is decided and recorded: retire, or wire into the required doc-lint job. Not left as-is.
- If wired: the four failures above are resolved at their root (allowlist updated, or the check re-scoped so legitimately-mentioning files do not trip it), and the script exits 0 on pristine main. A wired check that lands red is not acceptable.
- If wired: its own failure mode is proven by execution — mutating one allowed file to violate the property makes it exit non-zero on exactly that row.
- If retired: the file is deleted and the run-report that names it is left alone (it is a descriptive record of a past run and must not be rewritten), while any live normative sentence that depends on the script existing is reconciled in the same change.
- The fourth failure — a live same-commit sentence lacking the run-report clause in its two-line window — is investigated on its own merits before either path is taken. It may be a genuine drift in an always-in-context doc rather than allowlist rot, and it would be the only one of the four that points at a real normative gap.
title: Chore: scripts/knowledge/tests/landing-verify.sh has been red since it landed and runs in no CI job — retire it or wire it
